README: The target profile for `pnpm score`. Rebuilt 2026-10-19 because the previous one was measured
off the board at the BOARD's resolution, not ours, and that made two of the six axes unreachable
by construction. Chasing them is what airbrushed the grass, the water and the wolf.
THE BUG: reference/mocks/gameplay-concepts.png is a smooth illustration drawn at roughly three
to four image pixels per one of ours, and at that size the board's hard steps are smeared over
three or four pixels. The `edges` test (|dLuma| > 24 between neighbours) therefore missed nearly
all of them and reported 4.50% -- HALF our own figure. The score told every painter the art was
too busy when the board is in fact twice as crisp as ours. Round 2 obeyed, and softened.
THE FIX: every crop is now decimated to OUR pixel density before it is profiled -- nearest only,
reading the centre of each cell, so no colour in a crop was invented by resampling. `edges` went
4.50 -> 18.91 and `texture` 28.32 -> 42.17. deep, keyline and spread barely moved, which is the
check that the method is sound: those three are distributional, they should not care about
resolution, and across decimation factors 1 to 6 they vary by under 2%.
WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE ART, and it is the opposite of what the last brief said: we are NOT too
busy. At edges 9.9 against 18.9 we sit at 0.52 -- too SMOOTH. The board is crisp pixel art with
hard, readable steps and a near-black keyline round everything. Use tone() to make a mass round
and lit, and keyline() on everything that meets the ground, but do not dissolve a step into a
gradient to chase a number. No number rewards that any more.
To rebuild: cut each rect below from the board, take every nth pixel, run `--board <dir>`.
REBUILDING IS NOW SAFE, and this paragraph replaces the warning that used to stand here. The
warning said: five of the six targets are the plain mean of `each`, but `variety` is a hand-set
2.60 standing in for a measured 93.91, so `--board` silently reverted it and every distance
ballooned past 0.8 with no change to a single pixel of art. Telling the next agent to put it
back by hand was never going to work -- the failure is silent, and the instruction to rebuild
sat two lines above the warning not to.
So the rule is enforced in code instead of asked for in prose. `pinned` below names the axes
that are judgements rather than measurements; `--board` keeps the stored `target` for those and
prints the mean it declined, and `--world` marks them with a `*` so nobody reads 2.60 as the
board's own figure. A rebuild now also PRESERVES every key in this file rather than writing a
fresh three-key object over it -- the old one deleted the README, the scale, the method notes
and the warning itself, which is the larger half of the same bug.
If you need to change a pinned value, change `target` here and say why in `pinned`. If you need
to unpin an axis, delete its entry and rebuild; that is a deliberate act and it will show up in
the diff, which is the whole point.

source.layout: 3072x2048, four 1536x1024 frames: Explore (0,0), Question (1536,0), Inspect (0,1024), Arrive (1536,1024)
source.sampling: nearest decimation by `n`, reading the centre of each cell; fractional n is rounded per output pixel
source.rects-are: x, y, w, h in board pixels, inside the world art and checked by eye to hold no HUD, dialogue or control chrome
source.inspect-frame: excluded: almost entirely UI, and its slivers of world are too small to profile

scale.how: Red's cloak is the only object drawn on both sides at a known size, so she is the ruler. Her cloak silhouette was isolated as a connected scarlet blob in each board frame and compared with ours (24 px across the hood, 37 rows crown to hem).

measured.explore: cloak 64 x 101 board px -> 2.67 by width, 2.73 by height, n = 2.70
measured.question: cloak 87 x 130 -> 3.63 by width, 3.51 by height, n = 3.57
measured.arrive: cloak 94 x 132 -> 3.92 by width, 3.57 by height, n = 3.75

scale.why-it-matters: The three frames are NOT at one zoom -- Explore is framed ~30% wider than Question and Arrive. The old profile averaged all three at board resolution, mixing scales as well as mis-measuring them. Rounding n to integers 3 and 4 (a first pass of this rebuild) put `edges` at 20.88; the exact scales give 18.91. The 9% difference is why the fractional values are used.

pinned.variety: Hand-set to 2.60, a reachable stretch from our own palette ceiling. The board measures 93.91 at our pixel density and 33.10 scaled to a camera frame, and both are unreachable by construction -- see `variety-is-not-the-board`. `--board` keeps this value and reports the mean it declined.

per-axis.deep: 25.71. Was 26.68; resolution barely touched it, so it was always trustworthy. We sit near 0.6-0.75 of it: the world wants more deep shade, chiefly a dark pool under every tree and object.
per-axis.keyline: 17.55. Was 18.95. Also always trustworthy. This is the near-black outline the board puts round everything -- keyline(), which keeps the hue, not a darker shade().
per-axis.spread: 60.12. Was 61.23. Real, and mostly downstream of deep and keyline.
per-axis.edges: 18.91. Was 4.50, measured through the board's own blur, which inverted the advice. We are at ~9.9, so the art needs HARDER steps, not softer. See `resolution-relative` -- do not chase the last 5% of this.
per-axis.texture: 42.17. Was 28.32, understated the same way. Local 16px variation inside a tile: what a keyline plus a real tonal ramp produces, and what a flat fill cannot fake.
per-axis.variety: 2.60, and this one is deliberately NOT the board's figure. See `variety-is-not-the-board`.

resolution-relative.what: Neither converges as the decimation factor grows -- they measure how different pixels n apart are, which keeps rising. On explore-nw, edges reads 4.18 / 11.92 / 19.23 / 25.50 / 30.48 / 35.15 at n = 1..6, and texture 27.4 / 37.5 / 43.2 / 45.3 / 47.7 / 49.9. Over the same range deep stays 27.5-28.0, keyline 19.5-20.0 and spread 56.9-57.6.
resolution-relative.so: These two targets are only meaningful because both sides are now at the same pixel density, and they inherit the ~5% uncertainty in the scale measurement above. Treat 18.91 and 42.17 as 19 +/- 1 and 42 +/- 2. Getting from 9.9 to ~17 is the real work and is unambiguous; grinding from 18.5 to 18.9 is fitting noise.
resolution-relative.not-aliasing: Checked: moving the sampling phase within the cell changes edges by under 0.3% (explore-nw 19.02/19.23/19.33 across three phases, question-forest 26.02-26.13 across four). Aliasing would swing. This is real structure.

variety-is-not-the-board.why-the-two-differ: The axis is distinct 5-bit colours per 1000 px, so it falls as area grows: the numerator saturates, the denominator does not. The crops are 35k-55k px and a camera frame is 399,360, so the raw figure is not comparable with anything we render. Fitting Heaps' law C(S) = 28.74 * S^0.4754 over the pooled board sample and evaluating at 399,360 px gives 33.10. The same fit on our own renders predicts their measured totals to within 0.6-18%.
variety-is-not-the-board.why-even-33-is-unreachable: 33.10 per 1000px over a 399,360-px frame is 13,217 distinct 5-bit colours in one screen. Our entire tile set, rendered as the whole 60x42 map, contains about 805. The board reaches its figure because it is a smooth illustration in which nearly every pixel is a unique blend -- that is not a palette, it is the absence of one. Nor is it only blend noise in the tail: after discarding one-off blends, the board still needs 3,285 colours to cover 95% of its pixels against our 202.
variety-is-not-the-board.what-2.60-is: A reachable stretch set from our own ceiling instead of the board's. The whole map's palette is ~805 distinct 5-bit colours and our richest camera frame has reached 834 (2.09 per 1000px); 2.60 asks for roughly 1,040, about a 25% broadening of the ramps actually in use. tone() supplies that with no soft gradient anywhere, because `edges` at 18.91 now demands hard steps at the same time. The two axes brace each other: a richer ramp with crisp steps moves both, a blur moves one and wrecks the other.
variety-is-not-the-board.do-not-score-the-whole-map-on-this-axis: `--whole` renders 2,580,480 px, 6.5x a camera frame, so its variety reads ~0.31 however good the art is. Judge composition and density there; judge variety at camera size.

superseded.old-method: The same five views, cropped at the board's own resolution (700x500 and similar) and profiled directly, with the three frames' different zooms averaged together.
superseded.what-it-cost: `edges` and `variety` were together ~60% of the spawn distance and ~73% of the whole-map distance, and both pointed the wrong way: edges said 'simplify' to art already softer than the board, and variety said 'add colours' in a way only a gradient could satisfy. Three agents independently found the measurement was off and optimised against it anyway.
superseded.distances-under-each-ruler: Measured on identical renders, 2026-10-19; the art did not change, only the ruler. spawn-red 0.738 -> 0.351, cottage 0.796 -> 0.536, stall 0.776 -> 0.453, whole map 1.003 -> 0.611. The drop is not progress. It is the two impossible targets being removed. What matters is that all six axes now point the same way -- every ratio is below 1 -- where before `edges` fought the other five.
